arxiv-2202-03395.title: The excursion set model a step beyond :Environmental dependence
arxiv-2202-03395.creator: Nicos Hiotelis
arxiv-2202-03395.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nicos Hiotelis. In terms of the excursion set model, we used Monte Carlo methods in order to study the non-Markovian stochastic evolution of the smoothed overdensity δ \delta at scale S S . For a Gaussian density field, smoothed by the top-hat filter, in real space, we used random walks, with the correct correlation between scales, in order to calculate constrained probabilities and to connect the number of structures with the overdensity of their environment.

arxiv-2304-03121.title: Furstenberg systems of pretentious and MRT multiplicative functions Thanks: The first author was supported by the Research Grant ELIDEK HFRI-NextGenerationEU-15689. The second author was supported by Narodowe Centrum Nauki grant UMO-2019/33/B/ST1/00364.
arxiv-2304-03121.creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Mariusz Lemańczyk, Thierry de la Rue
arxiv-2304-03121.description: Abstract . We prove structural results for measure preserving systems, called Furstenberg systems, naturally associated with bounded multiplicative functions. We show that for all pretentious multiplicative functions these systems always have rational discrete spectrum and, as a consequence, zero entropy.

arxiv-2307-13808.title: Watermarking Conditional Text Generation for AI Detection: Unveiling Challenges and a Semantic-Aware Watermark Remedy Thanks: Corresponding Author Affiliation: Yu Fu, Deyi Xiong, Yue Dong
arxiv-2307-13808.description: Abstract To mitigate potential risks associated with language models (LMs), recent AI detection research proposes incorporating watermarks into machine-generated text through random vocabulary restrictions and utilizing this information for detection. In this paper, we show that watermarking algorithms designed for LMs cannot be seamlessly applied to conditional text generation (CTG) tasks without a notable decline in downstream task performance.

arxiv-2401-02300.title: Collocation-based Robust Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks (CRVPINN)
arxiv-2401-02300.creator: Marcin Łoś 1 , Tomasz Służalec 1 , Paweł Maczuga 1 , Askold Vilkha 1 , Carlos Uriarte 2 , Maciej Paszyński 1
arxiv-2401-02300.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marcin Łoś 1 , Tomasz Służalec 1 , Paweł Maczuga 1 , Askold Vilkha 1 , Carlos Uriarte 2 , Maciej Paszyński 1. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have been successfully applied to solve Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Their loss function is founded on a strong residual minimization scheme. Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks (VPINNs) are their natural extension to weak variational settings.

arxiv-2404-12069.title: Developing Application Profiles for Enhancing Data and Workflows in Cultural Heritage Digitisation Processes
arxiv-2404-12069.creator: Sebastian Barzaghi, Ivan Heibi, Arianna Moretti, Silvio Peroni
arxiv-2404-12069.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Barzaghi, Ivan Heibi, Arianna Moretti, Silvio Peroni. As a result of the proliferation of 3D digitisation in the context of cultural heritage projects, digital assets and digitisation processes – being considered as proper research objects – must prioritise adherence to FAIR principles. Existing standards and ontologies, such as CIDOC-CRM, play a crucial role in this regard, but they are often over-engineered for the need of a particular application context, thus making their understanding and adoption difficult.

arxiv-2505-19644.title: STOPA: A Dataset of S ystematic Varia T ion O f Dee P fake A udio for Open-Set Source Tracing and Attribution
arxiv-2505-19644.creator: Anton, Manasi, Jagabandhu, Vishwanath Pratap, Tomi H, Kamil
arxiv-2505-19644.description: Abstract A key research area in deepfake speech detection is source tracing — determining the origin of synthesised utterances. The approaches may involve identifying the acoustic model (AM), vocoder model (VM), or other generation-specific parameters. However, progress is limited by the lack of a dedicated, systematically curated dataset.

arxiv-2602-04527.title: Graph-Based Audits for Meek Single Transferable Vote Elections
arxiv-2602-04527.creator: Edouard Heitzmann 1
arxiv-2602-04527.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Edouard Heitzmann 1. In the context of election security, a Risk-Limiting Audit (RLA) is a statistical framework that uses a minimal partial recount of the ballots to guarantee that the results of the election were correctly reported. A generalized RLA framework has remained elusive for algorithmic election rules such as the Single Transferable Vote (STV) rule, because of the dependence of these rules on the chronology of eliminations and elections leading to the outcome of the election.

pmc-10552439.title: The endometrial transcriptome transition preceding receptivity to embryo implantation in mice
pmc-10552439.creator: Hon Yeung Chan, Ha M. Tran, James Breen, John E. Schjenken, Sarah A. Robertson
pmc-10552439.description: BackgroundReceptivity of the uterus is essential for embryo implantation and progression of mammalian pregnancy. Acquisition of receptivity involves major molecular and cellular changes in the endometrial lining of the uterus from a non-receptive state at ovulation, to a receptive state several days later. The precise molecular mechanisms underlying this transition and their upstream regulators remain to be fully characterized.

pmc-10631653.title: Perceptual metrics for odorants: Learning from non-expert similarity feedback using machine learning
pmc-10631653.creator: Priyadarshini Kumari, Tarek Besold, Michael Spranger
pmc-10631653.description: Defining perceptual similarity metrics for odorant comparisons is crucial to understanding the mechanism of olfactory perception. Current methods in olfaction rely on molecular physicochemical features or discrete verbal descriptors (floral, burnt, etc.) to approximate perceptual (dis)similarity between odorants. However, structural or verbal descriptors alone are limited in modeling complex nuances of odor perception.

pmc-11503429.title: Psychometric Testing of an Arabic Version of the Attitude Toward Skin-to-Skin Contact Instrument among Women in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Cultural Validation Study
pmc-11503429.creator: Abeer Hawsawi, Ritin Fernandez, Maria Mackay, Ibrahim Alananzeh, Abbas Al Mutair, Richard Gray
pmc-11503429.description: Background/Objectives: The World Health Organization recommends skin-to-skin contact immediately after birth, yet the practice rate remains low in Saudi Arabia, impacting the health and well-being of mother–baby dyads. No previous studies have explored Saudi women’s attitudes toward skin-to-skin contact, a critical factor in developing strategies to increase its adoption.

pmc-11547685.title: Thermal Conductivity of AlSi10MnMg Alloy in Relation to Casting Technology and Heat Treatment Method
pmc-11547685.creator: Iva Nováková, Milan Jelínek, Martin Švec, Wenming Jiang
pmc-11547685.description: Nowadays, with the development of electromobility, the requirements not only for the mechanical properties but also for the thermal conductivity of castings are increasing. This paper investigates the influence of casting and heat treatment technology on the thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity of an AlSi10MnMg alloy.

pmc-12542511.title: Ten-year outcomes of antiretroviral therapy: a retrospective cohort study in Tshwane district, South Africa
pmc-12542511.creator: Kateko Mhlongo, Murray Louw, Sanele Ngcobo
pmc-12542511.description: BackgroundSouth Africa continues to face one of the world’s highest HIV burdens, with 7.7 million people living with HIV (PLWHIV) in 2023. Despite progress toward UNAIDS 95–95–95 targets, challenges in long-term retention and treatment outcomes persist. This study aimed to evaluate 10-year antiretroviral therapy (ART) outcomes among PLWHIV initiated on treatment in 2013 within Tshwane District, South Africa.

pmc-12691095.title: CBCT-Based Retrospective Analysis of Posterior Superior Alveolar Artery Anatomy in a Saudi Population
pmc-12691095.creator: Abdullah Alqhtani, Amirah Yahya Alhaidan, Asma Jumah Aloufi, Faten Sifran Alharbi, Lama Mohammed Alkahtani, Raghad Hatem Alamri, Mohamed Omar Elboraey, Yiu Yan Leung
pmc-12691095.description: Background/Objectives: Sinus elevation in the posterior maxilla carries a risk of hemorrhage due to injury of the posterior superior alveolar artery (PSAA). Accurate preoperative identification of the PSAA using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) can enhance surgical safety. This retrospective study evaluated the prevalence, location, diameter, and visibility of the PSAA in a Saudi population.

pmc-12996815.title: Alexander disease mutations differentially sensitize glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) to posttranslational modifications and network disruption by oxidants
pmc-12996815.creator: Nuria Goya-Iglesias, Per Hägglund, Paula Martínez-Cenalmor, Tina Nybo, Lasse G Lorentzen, María A Pajares, Michael J Davies, Dolores Pérez-Sala
pmc-12996815.description: The type III intermediate filament protein glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) plays a key role in astrocyte and brain homeostasis. Mutations in GFAP can result in Alexander's disease (AxD), a severe neurodegenerative disease. Studies on AxD models indicate that oxidative stress may be an important pathogenic factor.

pmc-13145119.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026OT166 SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF EARLY ASPIRIN ADMINISTRATION AFTER INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS FOR ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE (TREND-IVT): A MULTICENTER, RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL

pmc-13145119.description: Background and aimsEarly neurological deterioration after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) occurs frequently in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and is associated with poor functional outcomes. Whether early initiation of antiplatelet therapy after IVT can improve recovery without increasing bleeding risk remains uncertain.

pmc-13156616.creator: Chuan Huang, Xinlan Zhang, Jia Ying, Ashley Fontana, Xiaohua Yang, Steven West, Paul Vaska, Sean AP Clouston, Benjamin J Luft

Diagnosis typically requires slit-lamp biomicroscopy, creating a significant access bottleneck in primary care and rural settings.
